Pattern: fly; fly to/with + N
Examples: They fly once a year and feel guilty about it. | She flew for the first time at fifty-two.

Pattern: land; land at + N
Examples: The plane landed nine hours late. | They landed in fog and waited on the tarmac.

Pattern: roam + N; roam around + N
Examples: They roamed the hills for a fortnight. | Goats roam the whole headland.

Pattern: venture into/out + N
Examples: Few visitors venture beyond the harbour. | They ventured inland and found the better walking.

Pattern: linger; linger over + N
Examples: They lingered over lunch until the heat passed. | Nobody lingers in a town with no benches.

Pattern: a crowded + N (beach, square)
Examples: The beach is crowded for nine weeks and empty for forty. | A crowded square at midnight suits nobody living above it.

Pattern: a deserted + N (street, resort)
Examples: The resort is deserted by October. | A deserted promenade in winter has its own appeal.

Pattern: a sun-drenched + N (coast, terrace)
Examples: The sun-drenched terrace is unusable by noon. | Brochures promise a sun-drenched coast and mention no wind.

Pattern: a family-friendly + N (resort, hotel)
Examples: The hotel is family-friendly in the useful sense: it has a kettle. | Family-friendly resorts fill up first in the holidays.

Pattern: a year-round + N (trade, service)
Examples: Year-round trade would change the whole economy here. | Only two hotels stay open on a year-round basis.

Pattern: a reasonably priced + N (room, meal)
Examples: A reasonably priced room is harder to find than a good one. | The meal was reasonably priced and generous.

Pattern: be overbooked; an overbooked + N
Examples: The flight was overbooked by nine seats. | An overbooked hotel moves you somewhere worse.

Pattern: be + fully booked
Examples: The campsite is fully booked from June. | Every guesthouse was fully booked for the festival.

Pattern: be/feel + jet-lagged
Examples: She was jet-lagged for the whole conference. | They arrived jet-lagged and went straight to work.

Pattern: be/get + sunburnt
Examples: He got sunburnt on the first afternoon. | Sunburnt shoulders are the local souvenir.

Pattern: head off; head off for + N
Examples: They headed off before the traffic built up. | She headed off for the coast with no booking.

Pattern: get in; get in at + giờ
Examples: They got in at two in the morning. | The coach gets in before the shops open.

Pattern: lay on + N hoặc lay + N + on; tách được
Examples: They laid on extra buses for the festival. | The hotel laid a cold supper on for late arrivals.

Pattern: put up at + N; không tách được
Examples: They put up at a guesthouse near the station. | He put up at the same hostel for a month.

Pattern: make for + N; không tách được
Examples: They made for the harbour as soon as it cleared. | Most visitors make for the castle and miss the rest.

Pattern: turn up; không có tân ngữ
Examples: They turned up without a booking and got the last room. | Nine people turned up for a tour built for forty.

Pattern: see out + N hoặc see + N + out; tách được
Examples: They saw out the fortnight in the rain. | He saw the season out and never returned.

Pattern: hang around; hang around + N
Examples: They hung around the quay waiting for the tide. | Nobody wants to hang around an airport for nine hours.

Pattern: stock up on + N; không tách được
Examples: They stocked up on water before the walk. | Visitors stock up on the cheese and take it home.

Definition: rốt cuộc lại ở đâu đó
Pattern: wind up + in/at + N
Examples: They wound up in a village with one bus a day. | He wound up at the same campsite three years running.

Pattern: hit the beach
Examples: They hit the beach before the coaches arrived. | Everyone hits the beach on the first warm day.

Pattern: pay/make + a flying visit
Examples: She paid a flying visit on her way north. | A flying visit of two hours is not a holiday.

Definition: dành cả ngày cho việc đó
Pattern: make a day of it
Examples: They packed a picnic and made a day of it. | If the weather holds we shall make a day of it.

Pattern: come/travel + from far and wide
Examples: Visitors come from far and wide for that one week. | The choir is known far and wide.

Pattern: be + worth the detour
Examples: The chapel is worth the detour and the climb. | Nine kilometres of poor road, and worth the detour.

Pattern: live in + the lap of luxury
Examples: The brochure promises the lap of luxury and delivers a kettle. | They lived in the lap of luxury for four nights.

Pattern: catch the sun
Examples: He caught the sun badly on the ferry deck. | She caught the sun in ten minutes.

Pattern: recharge one's batteries
Examples: A fortnight away recharged her batteries completely. | He goes walking to recharge his batteries.

Pattern: be in + the back of beyond
Examples: The cottage is in the back of beyond and has no signal. | They drove to the back of beyond for the quiet.

Pattern: see the world
Examples: He joined the merchant navy to see the world. | She saw the world on a nurse's wage.
